node.title: DLI first-junction split-Pell normal form
node.statement: Let n=2h, t=2L and interpolate the antipodal-pair values A(y_i)=a_i+b_i-1 and W(y_i)=x_i(a_i-b_i) on the order-h subgroup y_i=x_i^2. The first t moments vanish iff deg A<=h-L-1, W(0)=0, and deg W<=h-L. The binary alphabet is equivalent to Y^h-1 dividing A(A^2-1) and W^2+YA^2-Y. These conditions have an exact converse, and antipodal primitivity is exactly W!=0. Thus Z_0-C_1 is the nonzero-W split-Pell pair count. For L<=h/2 the Pell quotient has degree at most h-2L; for L>h/2 its numerator vanishes identically.
node.attack_surface: Check the one-degree even/odd interpolation asymmetry, the half-character factor in W, both polynomial congruences, converse sign reconstruction, owner equivalence, and quotient-degree arithmetic.
node.falsifier: A binary word whose moment prefix disagrees with the degree gaps, a split-Pell pair that does not recover a unique binary word, or an antipodally invariant word with W nonzero.
node.notes: This converts the truncated primitive prefix into a concrete bounded-degree polynomial classification problem. It does not count the pairs or control the deeper tower.
